title: Article. Balancing Risk and Return: The Simple Statistics of Investing
summary:
And so without further ado,
This week's memo is titled, balancing risk and return. The flawed implication is that taking on more risk can reliably generate higher return. Of course, though, if this
if this was true, then taking on more risk, wouldn't actually be risky.

reader_summary.overview: Hello and welcome to The Synopsis, a Speedwell Research podcast. I'm Drew Cohen, and this week on the synopsis, we will be reading one of our weekly memos. If this is your first time listening to the synopsis, we usually have four different show formats.

key_points.text: We have in-depth company episodes where we focus on a single business drawing from Speedwell Research's in-depth research reports.
key_points.evidence_quote: We have in-depth company episodes where we focus on a single business drawing from Speedwell Research's in-depth research reports, which you can buy at Speedwell Research.com, or second episode format is a dialogue podcast where we talk about various business and investing concepts.

key_points.text: Our third episode format are interviews.
key_points.evidence_quote: Our third episode format are interviews.

key_points.text: And what you are listening to right now is our fourth sort of episode, which is called an article podcast.
key_points.evidence_quote: And what you are listening to right now is our fourth sort of episode, which is called an article podcast, where we read our weekly memo for those that prefer to listen to it instead of reading it.

key_points.text: If you do want to read it instead, though, just go to Speedwell memos.com.
